concepts.quote: d = i happens by itself because double is bigger
concepts.why: States correctly that double is a wider type than int so an int widens into it, but computes no double values or operations in the code.
Correctly relates int to double: a double value becomes an int only through an explicit cast, applied to line int j = (int) 9.99 (truncation itself not mentioned).

concepts.quote: d = i happens by itself because double is bigger; going from 9.99 to int needs (int)
concepts.why: Identifies both conversion directions in the code and explains them by the types' ranges: widening int to double is automatic, narrowing double to int needs a cast.
Applies to this code the rule that a value outside a variable's type (a double into an int) is accepted only with a cast, while an int fits a double variable.
